targets.recommended_evidence_quality_note: V3-EXQ-946 (2026-08-23, PASS/adjudication=vacuous_pass) measured write-ADDRESS informativeness (not occupancy) at 4 operating points against a purpose-built blockwise-permutation order-only null, on a real REEAgent. BIAS_W1_0 (default weight) clears robustly (5/5 seeds, z 2.19-7.73); BIAS_W0_1 clears at the required floor (3/5 seeds, z -- one seed at 0.39, essentially null); BIAS_W0_01 and REFRACTORY do not clear (1/5, 2/5). The indexer's mechanical vacuous_pass flag is very likely a FALSE POSITIVE -- see Section 6 of the companion .md -- because the driver's own semantics is an explicit OR across 4 individually load_bearing:true per-arm criteria ('PASS iff AT LEAST ONE arm clears its bar'), and rule (3b) (build_experiment_indexes.py:532-539) fires unconditionally on any load_bearing:true+passed:false entry with no representation of run-level AND-vs-OR combination semantics. This is a distinct failure mode from the four already-documented join-mismatch sub-cases (branch-selector, criteria-tag join, aggregate _non_degenerate licence, arm::check convention), none of which are even reached here -- they live in the indexer's legacy fallback path, which (3b) short-circuits before it can run. Independently of the flag, the substantive finding is that the statistically real signal at BIAS_W1_0/W0_1 is of MINUTE magnitude: 0.0002-0.0006 bits against the same instrument's own 1.0-bit positive control (~0.02-0.06%). 'Distinguishable from an order-only null' is not 'carries usable context' -- reading this as closing the corrupting write-path defect would repeat the category error the 922a autopsy caught for MECH-152's prior FAILs. Recommend NOT flipping substrate_queue entry contextmemory-write-path-addressing-degeneracy to implemented_validated on this evidence alone.

learning_extracted: Write-address informativeness (distinct from occupancy, V3-EXQ-943's question) is statistically detectable at 2 of 4 operating points against a purpose-built, independently-validated order-only null, on a real agent -- the first run in this six-generation lineage to clear that specific bar with a null construction robust to the period-alignment artifact that produced false positives before.

The detectable signal is of minute magnitude (~0.02-0.06% of the instrument's own positive-control range) -- statistically real, practically negligible for any downstream differentiation DV until shown otherwise.

The seeds-clearing-null count falls strictly monotonically as bias_weight falls (5/5 -> 3/5 -> 1/5), the OPPOSITE direction from the driver's own stated hypothesis (weakening the usage term should let more content signal through), with sharply increased per-seed z-score variance at the lowest weight; BIAS_W0_01 additionally shows partial occupancy re-degeneration (4-14/16 slots).

REFRACTORY (content-only argmin, no usage term at all) underperforms BIAS_W1_0 on THIS instrument, the opposite ranking from a separate synthetic depth-based probe (mech152_writepath_addressing_probe_20260825.md) -- the two instruments disagree on which write-address mode is 'better', and per that probe's own stated preference this real-agent, order-only-null-validated result should be weighted over the synthetic one.

The indexer's vacuous_pass adjudication flag (rule 3b, build_experiment_indexes.py:532-539) fires unconditionally on any load_bearing:true+passed:false criterion with no representation of run-level AND-vs-OR combination semantics -- distinct in kind from the four documented join-mismatch sub-cases (V3-EXQ-783/906/908 etc., which are key-matching mismatches in the indexer's legacy fallback path, never reached once rule 3b fires).
